items.title: How confident can you be that an omission was deliberate?
items.description: Illustrative teaching model, not a real measurement: confidence that credit-stealing was deliberate (not an oversight) grows both with how directly the wording claims authorship and with how many times the same colleague has done it. At the Scenario's own numbers — an explicit claim ("the approach I came up with") on the first known instance — the model lands around 60: a fairly clear case, but, per L3, 'not with full certainty.' Drag repeat count up to see why a second or third instance makes the pattern itself the evidence, without any single incident needing to be airtight.

params.name: wordingStrength
params.label: How directly the wording claims authorship (0 = passive omission, 100 = explicit "I came up with this")

params.name: repeatCount
params.label: Times the same colleague has done this before (0 = this is the first known instance)
